I've thought of many things to say about this gem, but I'll try to keep it simple: this is the most underrated game I've ever played.

If you're the type of player that likes to challenge yourself and hone your skills, and you like retro graphics, then you will absolutely love this game.

In TowerClimb, you can have an exciting 2-3 hour session where you're really focused, but it's also great for casually playing for 5-10 minutes just to pass time. 

The gameplay is really deep and well-planned. There are many ways you can creatively overcome obstacles, but at the same time the game feels simple. Few games manage to pull this off. The charming graphics, sounds and music create a cozy, yet scary atmosphere that draws you in while fitting the challenging nature of the game.

The tower has many intriguing mysteries, guaranteed to sparkle your curiosity. But you can't just go ahead and explore them, because it's extremely dangerous. One mistake, and you could end up in floor 1 again. Which makes the mysteries so exciting! You have moments of tension where you think "should I go in there? seems dangerous... but I wonder what's inside that door!" And the game rewards you properly for your trouble. It's not just silly easter eggs or useless items. The secret areas reward you with a lot of great stuff, new content, new music, game modes, etc.

One last thing: this game even has a great, wholesome community, where people share their experiences and motivate each other to beat the game.

TowerClimb was made with a lot of passion. I hope you give it a try!

If you like fun & challenging games then this could be a rogue like for you! But, keep in mind everyone has their own tastes. Even within specific genres like rogue likes. Not only that some people like platformers where as others do not. Anyways I am 10 hours in (as of writing this), and I am having a blast with this game!

Though there was one gripe I had with this game. That is the overall controls. I honestly don't like what they provide for the keyboard, or my controllers (PS4 & XBOX ONE). Like with the controllers they force you to use the joystick, and you can not use the D-Pad natively. 

Though I did find a solution. That is using using a controller mapping software. Personally I use a software called Xpadder, but feel free to use what ever you want. That is in part why I am writing this review now before I complete the game. As a means to help other players with the game, and to hopefully motivate people to buy it. So don't let the bad native controls stop you from playing since there is a solution!

Also the controls are not in the options. So if you are going to heed my words here are the controls. Map them how ever you see fit:

Arrow Keys = Movement
W = Inventory
X = Jump
Left Shift = Run
C = Throw
Space = Navigate Inventory

Then there are some hot keys for certain items.


A = Jump Potion
W = Explosive Potion
D = Teleportation Potion

A few tips. You have a main inventory. On the corner of the screen you can see which item you have selected. Pressing throw does just that, and will throw the item from your inventory. But, if you hold shift while you do this you will pull out, and hold said items instead. That is as long as you continue to hold that button. If you let go of the button you let go of the item. Also you can store items that you are grabbing by pressing throw.

From what I can tell the attack/use button, for a held weapon/item (Grappling Hook to give you an example), is the same as jump. So you have to jump first, and then press jump a second time, in the air, to use said weapon/item. Or, like with a sword, you can also just hold the jump button, and your character will use it after a moment goes by.

Now when you simply press jump your character will jump high up, but you can only go so far forward. If you hold run your character will jump forward a greater distance, but not as high. There is a little secret around this. Just press both buttons at the same time, and you will combine them. There are certain jumps that are far out, and high up. Normally you won't be able to make these jumps. But, by pressing run, and jump together you should be able to.

There are dark blue/purple berries in the game. When your character walks into them they consume them, and you will see a purple gas coming from your character. You can only have three of these at a time. If you grab a fourth one your character will explode. Now here is a tip to try to mitigate the risk of using up an extra jump by accident. When you climb to the corner of an edge you have to press jump to get up, and over. Again, sometimes your character will use one of these jump berries when you do this...

So here is the tip. If you jump to a ledge, and your character is up high enough, you can simply walk to the top without pressing the jump button. Now, after trying this, if your character does not walk up, and over, here is what you do. Do not jump while pressing up, but rather press forward in the direction your character is facing. Also hold the button, and do not press it. Doing this should help mitigate the risk of using a jump berry by accident.

Also, one last thing. If your character is grabbing the edge properly they will bend outwards, with an arch. When they are doing this you should be able to hold on without having to press anything. This is when you want to press the jump button. But, even then sometimes your character can still waste a jump.

Lastly you can throw a held item downwards, when jumping, to gain a little extra height. You can use this to reach ledges, and areas above, that are just a little bit out of normal reach.

In case you are curious here are my personal bindings. I have placed the Jump Potion to L1. Then the Explosive Potion to R1. And, the Teleportation Potion to circle. Lastly R2 is my throw button, and L2 is Space so that I can navigate my inventory, and menus more easily. Well I hope this helps some of you!

[h1]Desperately Convincing You to Buy TowerClimb[/h1]

Alright, here’s the deal. This is the first review I’m writing in like 10 years of buying games on Steam. I’m someone who plays as many roguelites as I can and always look for the games you can pour hundreds if not thousands of hours into; the FTLs, Isaacs, Slay The Spires, Spelunkys, etc. of the genre. Games you can more or less effectively come back to forever, like Solitaire or something. So when I look at reviews, I tend to pay attention to the average player time.

When I saw the reviews of TowerClimb, safe to say I was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ blown away. Almost everyone has 100+ hours, yet the game had a staggeringly low amount of reviews. You can check the New & Trending section for Roguelites right now and find countless new games with lower playtimes and less glowing reviews, but review counts that blow this games out of the water.

You might notice I’ve barely played the game, and it’s true, I’ve played for like an hour. I actually played it some years ago too, and ended up refunding it as I was pretty underwhelmed. But this time around, I had to see what it was that made it so repayable to people, and I found a video on YouTube called [b]“TowerClimb - Spelunky’s Deranged Cousin”.[/b] If you are interested in this game like I am, and don’t mind having some of its secrets (which realistically, you would have to look up to uncover, anyways) spoiled for you, I implore you to check it out. The amount this game has going for it is staggering and absolutely unexpected based on this store page. To get to the game’s “Legendary” ending, you have to undergo a rigoruous series of challenges to collect several shards, and one of them involves [b]playing the Regular Ending’s final boss in a 1v1 game of basketball, minigame that appears nowhere else in the game. You can then keep the basketball in your inventory for the rest of your run and dribble it to use as a weapon.[/b] And most players will probably never see it, even after playing for dozens of hours and beating the main game. That is the level depth and content at play in TowerClimb, and if I hadn’t watched that video, I would have thought this game was 1% as deep as it actually is. 

This game needs more love. It has less than 300 reviews on Steam after having been released for nearly 10 YEARS at the time of writing this. The developer was planning to add even MORE content to the already staggering amount in the form of a third chapter, but no news has been heard for years. If this game gets more attention and blows up, there’s a chance it might still happen someday, and the game could even be ported to consoles, get proper Steam Deck support (don’t worry I played it on Deck fine after 5 mins of tinkering, just need to look up how to fix Towerclimb using Protonfix with a guide online), etc. Please buy it for yourself. As I’m writing this all I can think about is how eager I am l to pour countless hours into this game and explore all it has to offer.

What a gem! This game has so much more depth than a quick glance would convey. It starts off simple enough, but grows in complexity very quickly. From the very first level though, the immense difficulty of this game makes itself known. If you aren't willing to go through being eviscerated, incinerated, crushed, eaten, electrocuted, stabbed, and so, so many other horrible fates over, and over again, you won't progress in this game. My first victory took me 126 hours of play, and that was only the simplest ending. I still have yet to see everything this game has to offer.

The controls are tricky to get used to, and sometimes seem confusing, but with practice, they become second nature. The music is heavy with atmosphere, and conveys great weight to your journey. The visuals are simple, but effective. For some people the graphics may be a turn off, and some parts of the game aren't the prettiest, but on the whole, there's a surprising amount of detail in the game despite the low resolution pixel art. This becomes more apparent later on in the game.

TL;DR
Gameplay is deep
Difficulty is extreme
Music is cool
Graphics are simple, but get the job done
I'd highly recommend checking this one out if you're a fan of other rouguelikes, especially Spelunky.

A well-polished and interesting game with extremely clunky controls, likely abandoned by the developer. First off, this game is VERY punishing - one hit from anything results in instant death (even just falling from too high of a platform) and will send you back to the beginning of the game. This isn't a downside though; many punishing games can be rewarding for skilled players. However, I prefer if the difficulty comes from the gameplay rather than the CONTROLS. To swing a sword, you press the Jump button (yes, it will also make you jump). To hold something, you have to hold down X the ENTIRE time because if you ever let it go, the item in your hands will be violently flung away from you. Did I mention X is also the Run button? Additionally, there's no pause button whatsoever and the developer has expressed his dislike of them - good luck if anything ever requires your immediate attention in real life. This is a game that does not respect your time.

One thing that really strikes me as unusual is that this game actually has lots of hidden content that 99% of the playerbase will almost never see due to the base games difficulty. It seems like the developer finished the first two chapters and then spent all his time adding optional content behind it, but it feels pointless because only the most dedicated, adderall-infused, diehard gamers will actually manage to see any of it. The Boiler Room? The Colosseum? Seeing the final boss in basketball jersey and dunking on him in a basketball match? All this developer effort spent on things almost nobody will ever experience. It's honestly a shame.

I've heard people call it "reverse Spelunky," but that feels overly reductive. In Spelunky, you're going downwards, and gravity is on your side. Here, a decent chunk of the game is just solving the problem of "How do I go up?" because gravity is very much your enemy. The title is pretty literal - you climb a tower, that's the focus of the game. (A real shocker, I know.) Everything else is just a wrench in the gears of your plans to go higher, or another cog to build them with.

It's also a fair bit more technical than most games - there's a few moves that feel like I'm describing fighting game combos. I frequently fall to my death because I pressed the wrong button (RB/X) for Throw Item (LB) or just whiffed the wall-grab because I was too slow or held Sprint (which turns "Throw" into "Hold") or whatever else can go wrong with trying to item-hop around an overhang.

It does have an easy mode, although it's not a huge concession - 3 health instead of 2. I assume it makes a fairly big difference in how far you can go, but it's still no easier to do anything in particular... You just get an extra mulligan on that item-hop where you accidentally took out a crate and lovingly embraced it as you plummeted to your death instead of tossing it into the uncaring abyss to save yourself.

And a word of warning: Don't pet the dogs.

I tried picking this up a few times and never got past the first 30 minutes of gameplay because it seemed pretty repetitive. After finally sitting down and powering through it I discovered an absolute gem.

It's an absurdly difficult game, but mastering the mechanics completely alleviates that. Any time you die, it is 100% your fault. There's a lot to them aswell, from chaining item throws to ascend higher than what a single item throw would let you, to throwing an item and boomerang at the same time to get the extra height and have the boomerang recover the item you used, to the extremely finnicky mobility items that are just as likely to get you killed but let you go dangerously fast.

The true ending took me about 80 hours of grinding to achieve (with a single full run only taking about an hour), which involves starting from the beginning and visiting a few secret areas that each have an item you need to carry to the end of the game. Having to haul these severely limits your inventory space which further compounds the difficulty as you have less room for important tools to help navigate. It was an extremely rewarding journey to go through, and now I'm able to chain multiple wins together back to back.

On top of that, there are some awesome locations to experience that I highly encourage being completely blind on. The game also sports a fantastic soundtrack, a lot of which has made it's way into mine and a few friends playlists.
